beats.caption: This is CraftV. It puts real Minecraft inside GTA V.
You play as Steve, with your hotbar, your hearts and your hunger, right on the streets of Los Santos.
You can build anywhere, blow up cars with TNT, and bring your friends along.
Setting it up takes about fifteen minutes, and I'll walk you through every step.
Quick, but important. This is for story mode only.
Never take mods into GTA Online. You can get your account banned, and CraftV switches itself off if it even sees an online session.
Here's what you'll need. Your own copy of GTA V Legacy, and Minecraft Java Edition.
Then a few free tools. Script Hook V, ReShade, and Fabric for Minecraft.
And CraftV itself. Every link is in the description. Only grab them from those official sites.
Part one is GTA. Start with Script Hook V. Open the zip, and go into the bin folder.
Drag these two files into your GTA folder. That's the one with GTA5.exe in it.
Now unzip CraftV, and drop CraftV.asi and the .ini file right next to them.
Next up, ReShade. This is what draws Minecraft into GTA's picture.
On reshade.me, pick the version with full add-on support. The normal one won't work.
In the installer, choose GTA5.exe, then DirectX 10/11/12.
When it offers effect packs, untick all of them. CraftV brings its own.
Now, this is the step everyone misses. Find dxgi.dll in your GTA folder,
and rename it to ReShade64.asi. That's how Script Hook V knows to load it.
Last thing for GTA. Copy everything from the "Minecraft view" folder in the CraftV zip into your game folder.
Part two, Minecraft. CraftV runs its own copy of Minecraft next to GTA, using your normal account.
Run the Fabric installer, pick version 26.3, and hit Install.
In the Minecraft Launcher, open installations, and edit the new Fabric one.
Give it its own game folder. That way your normal Minecraft stays exactly how it is.
Inside that folder, make a mods folder, and drop in Fabric API and the CraftV mod.
Part three is quick. In GTA's graphics settings, set the screen type to Windowed Borderless.
And turn off "Pause Game On Focus Loss", so GTA keeps running next to Minecraft.
And that's the setup. Every time you play, start the Fabric version of Minecraft first. It opens a world called CraftV by itself.
Leave it running, start GTA, and load story mode.
When the little CraftV box in the corner says "MC view", you're in.
Left click breaks blocks and hits things. People react, and cars dent.
Right click places blocks, eats food, and pulls back your bow.
E opens your inventory, Space does a Minecraft jump, and F8 opens the settings.
The settings menu looks just like GTA's. Turn the crosshair on or off, hide your hand, change the frame rate,
pick whether Steve sits in cars, and switch damage, TNT and torch light on or off. If your FPS drops, lower the quality here.
Want to play with friends? Your address is in that same menu, under "Friends join at".
Friends with normal Minecraft just join that address from multiplayer.
Friends with their own GTA install everything too, and put your address in one config file. Then you see each other in Los Santos.
If they're not on your Wi-Fi, forward port 25565 on your router.
If you don't see the CraftV box at all, Script Hook V isn't loading. Check its files are next to GTA5.exe.
If the box shows up but Minecraft doesn't, check the ReShade rename, and make sure Minecraft started first.
Still stuck? Open an issue on the GitHub page with your log files.
That's it. Go build something ridiculous in Los Santos. And remember, story mode only. Have fun.
